previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, chronic heart failure, diabetes, and long-term anticoagulation was admitted for a painful right axillary abscess. She reported a one-week history of a growing lump and subjective fevers. Imaging confirmed a 4.8 cm fluid collection, and she underwent ultrasound-guided aspiration, yielding 20 cc of pus. Cultures grew Morganella morganii, resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, with mixed flora on gram stain. Due to persistent fluid on follow-up ultrasound, she underwent incision and drainage. Antibiotics were adjusted from vancomycin to piperacillin-tazobactam and then transitioned to oral doxycycline, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole. Warfarin was held initially, then restarted with heparin bridging, achieving a therapeutic INR by discharge. Her chronic conditions were managed without complication. She was discharged home with oral antibiotics, pain control, dressing changes, and home health support.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with refractory polymyositis with ? pulmonary 
involvement, h/o DVT/PE, morbid obesity, now presenting to ED 
with low grade fever, generalized weakness, dyspnea, cough.

#Cough/dyspnea: Most likely due to viral process.  There was a 
component of mild acute diastolic heart failure as well which 
resolved with IV lasix x 1 dose and resuming home lasix dose 
40mg BID.  Workup for bacterial infection was negative (chest 
XRAY, UA, blood cultures).  She improved with supportive care.  

#Polymyositis: Progressive.  She has significant deconditioning 
from this chronic disorder, her acute illness as above, as well 
as a component of steroid myopathy.  Rheumatology was consulted. 
 She was continued on chronic steroids (with Ca, Vit D, 
alendronate and bactrim for Pneumocystis prophylaxis).  Once her 
workup for bacterial infection was negative x 48 hours, she was 
started on CellCept.  Her starting dose is 500 mg daily (start: 
___.  This should be increased by 500 mg daily every 7 days 
(500mg BID starting ___, then 1000mg QAM +500mg QPM on ___ to 
a final dose of 1,000 mg BID, starting ___.  She will need 
weekly safety labs during this titration period: CBC, BUN/Cr, 
LFTs to be faxed to her rheumatologist  . Results to MD on call 
and to Dr ___ phone ___. 

#h/o DVT/PE:  The patient self discontinued her warfarin at 
home, but after discussion of risks/benefits was willing to 
re-start.  She was initially started on a heparin drip.  
However, she has poor IV access, and we were unable to monitor 
PTT q6hours while on heparin.  The IV nurses were unable to 
place a bedside PICC for access and the patient's weight exceeds 
the limit for ___ placement.  Her weight exceeds the threshold 
for lovenox (though she states she has received this medication 
previously).  In discussion with Pharmacy, Fondaparinox 10 mg sc 
daily was started.  Given her weight, this may be slightly 
underdosed however there is no data for higher dosing levels. 
The alternative would be to place a central line (triple lumen) 
for a heparin drip. The risks and benefits of this were 
discussed with the patient.  She agreed with the plan to use 
fondaparinox.  She was given coumadin 12.5 mg on ___ and ___ 
and then restarted on her home regimen: 7.5mg on ___, 
___ and 10mg on the other four days.  She will 
need her INR monitored every other day while at rehab.  
Fondaparinox should be discontinued once INR = ___ for ___ 
hours.  Pt's INR 1.9 on ___ and 2.8 on ___ which may have been 
spurious as prior labs were consistently 1.6.

#Axillary abscess with ? sinus tract: Treated on prior 
admission.  No evidence of active infection seen on this 
admission.
.
#hypoxemia-chronic. Pt reports use of 2L nC at night and 
intermittently during the day prn. Likely related to chronic 
PE?, OSA, vs. obesity hypoventilation, +known interstitial lung 
disease. Last echo ___ was normal. Should follow up with her 
outpatient pulmonologist Dr. ___ discharge from rehab 
and for consideration of outpt sleep study as it is unclear from 
last clinic note, if patient was able to do so.
.
#incidental radiographic findings-CXR read states ""unchanged 
peribronchovascular opacities as seen on multiple prior chest 
x-rays and CTs. No new areas of focal consolidation. However, 
more subtle pneumonia cannot be excluded"". Pt did not have 
symptoms of a clinical bacterial pneumonia. Symptoms as above 
resolved without antibiotic treatment. Likely a factor to 
chronic hypoxia. Likely related to known ILD. Pt should follow 
up with her pulmonologist as above
. 
#urinary tract infection/cystitis- Completed cefpodoxime x3 
days, as Ecoli resistant to bactrim and cipro.
.  
#morbid obesity-outpt f/u. Can discuss nutition referral and
